title: Pause & Deserve
tagline: Solo horror prototype—built in 8 weeks to learn Unreal. Pause freezes the enemy, but each use makes it permanently faster.

gameplay.title: Core Concept
gameplay.desc: A horror game built on a risk-reward loop where safety now equals difficulty later. I built this solo in 8 weeks as a learning project—wanted to prove I could handle both code and audio implementation in Unreal Engine 5. The point wasn't to build something complex—it was to prove I could ship a complete game alone.

soundscape.title: Forest Ambience
soundscape.desc: Forest ambience with randomized sounds—rustling grass, snapping twigs. Nothing complex, but enough to make the forest feel alive and keep you on edge.
soundscape.oppressive_desc: Freezing time plays a ticking clock sample—simple tension builder to remind you the pause won't last forever.
soundscape.proximity_desc: The enemy is visible, so audio isn't critical for tracking. But footsteps and breathing add to the tension when it gets close.
soundscape.environmental_desc: Randomized ambient emitters (twigs snapping, leaves rustling) trigger around the player to create false positives and tension.

audio_system.title: Technical Implementation
audio_system.desc: Native Unreal audio—MetaSounds and Sound Cues. Library music. The goal was learning the engine, not building a complex audio system.
audio_system.pause_desc: When you pause, a ticking clock plays. That's it—no fancy ducking or mix changes. Simple and effective.
audio_system.threat_desc: Music is from a library—atmospheric horror tracks. No adaptive layers, just well-chosen loops that fit the mood.
audio_system.spatial_desc: Used UE5's HRTF for immersive forest ambience—footsteps and ambient sounds feel like they come from around you.

tension.title: Development Insights
tension.desc: This project taught me the value of scope. By limiting mechanics to movement and one ability (Time Freeze), I could polish the audio-visual feedback loop to a high standard.
tension.subbass_desc: Simple, high-quality samples worked better than complex synthesis. Good foley and reliable spatialization carried the experience.
tension.silence_desc: I would implement proper audio occlusion (diffraction) around geometry and distinct reverb zones for indoors/outdoors.
tension.misdirection_desc: Even in a simple prototype, audio sells the experience. The forest sounds make it feel real, even if the visuals are placeholder.

chase.title: AI Behavior
chase.desc: Simple nav-mesh based AI that patrols until line-of-sight is established, then pursues. Speed scales with player's ability usage.

pause.title: Time Mechanic
pause.desc: Pausing halts AI movement for 5s. Penalty: AI speed multiplier increases by +0.2x permanently per use. Max cap: 2.5x.

world.title: Level Design
world.desc: Linear progression: Forest entry -> Cabin (Key) -> Forest Escape. Environmental sounds hint at the path forward.

score.title: Game Loop
score.desc: Explore -> Locate Objective -> Survive Chase -> Escape. Checkpoints reset AI speed to keep the difficulty fair on retry.

design.title: Production
design.desc: 8-week timeline. Weeks 1-6: Greyboxing and Blueprint logic. Weeks 7-8: Audio implementation, lighting, and polish. Used placeholder assets until systems were stable.

tech.title: Under the Hood
tech.desc: Unreal Engine 5.1. Logic: 100% Blueprints. Audio: MetaSounds & Sound Cues. Version Control: Git/GitHub. Assets: Sourced and processed from libraries.
